title: Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-Aware Minimization
main_claims: SAM's per-step direction towards flat regions (the orthogonal component gv) changes slowly across iterations and can be reused periodically without significant accuracy loss.
LookSAM, which recomputes the flat-region-seeking direction only every k steps, achieves accuracy comparable to vanilla SAM while reducing training time substantially.
Look-LayerSAM (combining periodic updates with layer-wise perturbation scaling) enables ViT training at batch sizes up to 64k, setting a new speed record.
methodology: SAM's update direction is decomposed into gh (parallel to SGD gradient) and gv (orthogonal, pointing toward flatter regions). LookSAM recomputes gv every k steps and reuses it otherwise. The stability of gv across iterations is verified empirically and theoretically via Taylor expansion. Experiments cover ResNet-18/50, WideResNet on CIFAR-100, and ViT-B/S models on ImageNet-1k. Large-batch experiments use up to 1024 TPU-v3 chips.
key_results: LookSAM-5 achieves the same accuracy as vanilla SAM on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 (80.7%) and ViT-B-16/ImageNet (79.8%) while reducing training time by roughly 32% per epoch for ViT-B-16.
Look-LayerSAM scales ViT-B-16 training to 32k batch size with 77.1% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1k, completing training in 0.7 hours.
The gap between LookSAM and SAM-k (naive periodic SAM) is 0.6–1.0% on WideResNet-28-10/CIFAR-100, demonstrating the importance of reusing the projected component rather than simply skipping steps.
limitations: The efficiency analysis focuses on ViTs; whether LookSAM's accuracy-speed tradeoff holds for smaller CNN models under OOD conditions is not examined.
No OOD or corruption benchmark experiments (e.g. CIFAR-C) are included; only in-distribution accuracy is reported.
The theoretical stability bound for gv ignores third-order terms; how well this approximation holds in practice for different architectures is not fully characterized.
relevance_to_rq: Peripheral to the core RQ but relevant as a SAM variant: LookSAM's decomposition of SAM into a loss-descent and a flat-region component provides mechanistic insight into what SAM actually optimizes, but the paper does not study OOD generalization or compare to SWA.

key_quotes.text: the direction pointing to the flat region won't change significantly within a few iterations
key_quotes.context: Empirical motivation for reusing gv across iterations in LookSAM

key_quotes.text: LookSAM achieves similar accuracy gains to SAM while being tremendously faster - it enjoys comparable computational complexity with first-order optimizers such as SGD or Adam

Keskar et al. showed that the main challenge in large-batch training is the convergence to sharp local minima due to insufficient noise in first-order stochastic updates, and SAM is a natural remedy for this problem
key_quotes.context: Motivation linking SAM to the sharpness problem in large-batch training
